During an intense two-week December session, students will spend three days conducting research and analysis of the Chicago advertising, media, and public relations industry environment; then travel to New York for four days of visits to major agencies, organizations, and media outlets, as well as meet and present to industry leaders and professionals on a special topic selected by a New York agency. (0 credit hours) JOUR 245 | NEWS EDITING | 4 quarter hours (Undergraduate) This course introduces students to editing and publishing procedures, including content editing, copy editing, proofreading and headline writing for publications, including online media. Students will practice story organization, news judgment, brevity, ethics, grammar, usage, punctuation, AP style, basic layout, photo editing and headline writing. Students will analyze the editor's central role in the newsroom and the flow of a story from a reporter to the public. JOUR 275 is a prerequisite for this course. JOUR 275 | INTRODUCTION TO JOURNALISM | 4 quarter hours (Undergraduate) An introduction to the field of journalism. Instruction and practice in writing and reporting news stories. Students will learn the skills needed to become better communicators and to understand the news in the world around them. JOUR 276 | PHOTOJOURNALISM | 4 quarter hours (Undergraduate) Introduction to the theoretical and technical foundations of photography with exploration of the medium's aesthetic, documentary and narrative purposes. Cross-listed as ART 377. JOUR 278 | NEWS REPORTING | 4 quarter hours (Undergraduate) Students build on writing and reporting skills introduced in JOUR 275 Intro to Journalism with more practice and skills in newsgathering, interviewing, using visuals, and understanding additional journalism storytelling techniques. JOUR 275 is a prerequisite for this class. JOUR 279 | FEATURE WRITING | 4 quarter hours (Undergraduate) This class helps students develop observational and narrative skills essential to writing feature stories suitable for multiple platforms. Students will learn the story telling techniques that emphasize human interest, description and the details of a subject. Instruction will include interactive lectures, class discussions, writing exercises and critiques. JOUR 280
